title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Reference, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade and Rollback Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended practices, reference architectures, packaging notes, day-2 operational procedures, and upgrade/rollback playbooks for Private Deployments (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and customer-facing solutions engineers who own installing, operating, and upgrading private clusters.

Sections included:
- Scope and intended audience
- High-level reference architectures (VPC and on-prem)
- Packaging and installation checklist (cloud VPC and on-prem bundle)
- Day-2 operations: monitoring, backups, scaling, and common runbooks
- Upgrade strategy and step-by-step rollback procedures
- Customer requirements library: network/security/compliance checklist
- Validation and smoke tests for post-deploy and post-upgrade verification
- Owners and escalation contacts

1) Scope and audience
- Scope: Covers Redwood Private deployments using the Redwood control plane (optional private control plane) with data plane in customer VPC or on-prem air-gapped environments. Includes guidance for dedicated GPU nodes, autoscaling, and persistent state (metadata, metrics, and K/V caches).
- Audience: Deploy engineers, SREs, solutions engineers, customer infra teams, and platform security reviewers.

2) High-level reference architectures
- VPC Deployment (recommended for most customers):
  - Components: customer VPC (subnets: public for bastion, private for nodes), NAT gateway, EFS/NFS or customer-provided CSI storage, managed RDS or customer DB for control-plane metadata, Redis-compatible service for KV cache (optional), optional On-Prem GPU nodes via VPN/Direct Connect.
  - Network flows: HTTPS API traffic -> Internet LB -> Control plane / ingress. Internal routing via private subnets and RBAC enforced by security groups. Traffic to Redwood-managed observability endpoints can be proxied through the control plane or pushed via an agent.
  - Sizing guidance: start with 2 master/control-plane nodes (t3.medium equivalent) and 2 GPU worker nodes (e.g., A100/Trn-class depending on model). For production, recommend 3 control-plane nodes and a minimum of 4 GPU workers for capacity and HA.

- On-Prem / Air-gapped Deployment (for regulated customers):
  - Components: customer datacenter with VLANs for management, compute, and storage; on-prem K8s cluster (k8s 1.24+ supported), Redwood Operator, CSI for local storage, local NFS/ceph/backed long-term object store, optional HSM integration for KMS.
  - Networking: Private DNS, NTP, and internal CA. Optional outbound-only control-plane telemetry via customer-approved egress proxy.
  - Hardware guidance: GPU nodes should have NVLink where possible; target GPU memory that supports model KV cache sizes. See quantization-profiles for model memory targets.

Reference architecture diagrams (text):
- VPC: "Internet -> LB -> Control plane in private subnets -> GPU workers in private subnets -> CSI storage -> Object store"
- On-Prem: "Bastion -> On-prem K8s API -> Redwood Operator -> GPU nodes -> Local object store -> Local KMS/HSM"

3) Packaging and Installation checklist
- Pre-install checklist (customer-side):
  1. Network and firewall rules confirmed (see Customer requirements below).
  2. DNS entries and certificates prepared (wildcard or SAN certs).
  3. NTP and time sync validated across nodes.
  4. GPU driver and CUDA versions validated per runtime matrix.
  5. CSI storage mounted and permissions set.
  6. KMS/HSM integration details (if required) and secrets access approved.

- Installer artifacts included in the bundle:
  - installer.tar.gz (Redwood operator + manifests)
  - terraform/arm templates for VPC bootstrap (optional)
  - kustomize overlays for on-prem and VPC variants
  - upgrade-runbook.md and rollback-scripts.sh
  - preflight.sh for environment validation

- Example Terraform snippet (VPC bootstrap):
  ```hcl
  module "redwood_vpc" {
    source = "git::ssh://git.redwood.com/infra/terraform//modules/redwood-vpc"
    name   = "redwood-private-prod"
    cidr   = "10.20.0.0/16"
    region = "us-west-2"
  }
  ```

- Example k8s manifest snippet (operator):
  ```yaml
  apiVersion: apps/v1
  kind: Deployment
  metadata:
    name: redwood-operator
  spec:
    replicas: 2
    template:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: operator
          image: registry.redwood.com/operator:v2026.01.12
  ```

4) Day-2 operations (runbooks and playbooks)
- Monitoring and alerting baseline (SRE defaults):
  - Metrics to monitor: per-model latency P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, queue length, API error rate (4xx/5xx).
  - Baseline SLOs: API P95 latency < 300ms for short-form generation (<= 256 tokens) for Dedicated tier; availability 99.9%.
  - Alert thresholds: GPU utilization > 85% for 5m, KV cache hit rate < 40%, queue length > 1000, error rate > 1% over 5m.

- Common operational playbooks (short):
  - Service degradation (high latency):
    1. Confirm alerts in Grafana and traces in Jaeger.
    2. Identify hot-model via per-route dashboard.
    3. Apply temporary scaling policy: increase worker replicas or add pre-warmed nodes.
    4. If autoscale fails, enact manual node provisioning and move traffic to fallback model variant.
  - Cache corruption or KV mismatch:
    1. Quiesce the model route (set to degraded).
    2. Rotate cache by clearing cache namespace and warm with replay prompts.
    3. Validate outputs against golden prompt set in eval-harness.
  - Storage full / object store latency:
    1. Identify heavy consumers via usage dashboard.
    2. Initiate retention compaction or increase storage IO/throughput.

- Backups and restore:
  - Control-plane metadata: daily DB backups retained 30 days, incremental hourly snapshots (configurable).
  - KV cache: best-effort warmup; persistent cache should be backed by redis-snapshots if configured.
  - Procedure to restore metadata DB:
    1. Quiesce writes by setting cluster to read-only mode.
    2. Restore latest consistent snapshot to standby DB.
    3. Run schema migrations in dry-run, validate, then switch.

5) Upgrade strategy (supported during maintenance windows)
- Principles:
  - Minor patch upgrades (security/patch): can be rolled through in bunches with 10-20% canary traffic.
  - Minor feature releases: staged rollout with canary and automated validation.
  - Major upgrades (control-plane or k8s version bump): require full maintenance window, compatibility checks, and pre/post automated test run.

- Pre-upgrade steps (always run):
  1. Confirm preflight.sh all-pass and backups completed (metadata DB & storage snapshots).
  2. Record current manifests and image digests.
  3. Notify stakeholders and schedule maintenance window.
  4. Run smoke tests against staging mirror.

- Canary upgrade pattern (recommended):
  1. Deploy new operator image to 1 control-plane replica and 10% of workers.
  2. Route 5-10% production traffic to canary model routes.
  3. Run automated validation: unit smoke tests, end-to-end happy-path, golden prompt regressions (eval-harness).
  4. Monitor for 30-60 minutes (or 2x p95 of normal traffic) for errors and latencies.
  5. If green, increase to 50% then full rollout. If red, trigger rollback plan.

- Upgrade validation checklist (post-upgrade):
  - API health endpoints return OK
  - Per-model latency within 10% of baseline
  - No new 5xx rates above 0.1%
  - KV cache hit-rate not degraded by >5%
  - Storage IO and DB replication lag within expected range

6) Rollback procedures (fast, safe rollback matrix)
- Rollback triggers:
  - Canary or full rollout causes P95 > 2x baseline for >30 minutes
  - Error rate spikes > 0.5% sustained > 10 minutes
  - Data corruption confirmed or DB migration failure

- Immediate rollback steps:
  1. Pause rollout and mark cluster degraded.
  2. Revert Kubernetes manifests to recorded previous image digests (we keep last-3 revisions in operator).
  3. For control-plane DB issues, restore DB snapshot to standby (follow restore procedure).
  4. Re-run smoke tests and golden prompt checks.
  5. Communicate rollback in status channel and open incident for RCA.

- Safe rollback matrix (examples):
  - Non-destructive operator bug: scale down new pods, scale up previous replica set, prune new images.
  - DB migration failure: restore snapshot and re-apply migration on isolated staging; do not retry migrations on production until validated.
  - GPU runtime incompatibility: set node selector to previous GPU runtime pool and cordon/drain incompatible nodes.

7) Customer requirements library (network/security/compliance checklist)
- Network and firewall:
  - Required outbound ports: 443 (control-plane telemetry), 5000-6000 (internal gRPC ranges - optional), NTP (123), DNS (53).
  - DNS: internal FQDNs for control-plane endpoints and object store.
  - VPN/Direct Connect: configured for on-prem to cloud control-plane integrations.

- Security & identity:
  - TLS: TLS 1.2+ enforced. Wildcard or SAN certs recommended.
  - Auth: SSO (OIDC) integration for console; mTLS for service-to-service recommended for restricted setups.
  - Key management: HSM/KMS integration details required for restricted deployments.

- Storage and data residency:
  - Object store encryption at rest (SSE) and in transit (HTTPS).
  - Retention policy agreements and retention delete workflows must be documented prior to install.

- Compliance artifacts required prior to install:
  - SOC2 evidence for any managed components (if Redwood-run control plane requested).
  - Customer ATO checklist (if applicable).

8) Validation and smoke tests (post-deploy / post-upgrade)
- Smoke test list (automated):
  1. Health endpoint check: curl -sf https://api.<cluster>/health || fail
  2. Short generation end-to-end latency test: 10 requests of <=64 tokens and check p95 < 300ms baseline.
  3. Embeddings sanity: run 5 embeddings and assert cosine similarity > 0.95 for identical inputs.
  4. Eval harness golden prompts: run 20 golden prompts and compare to golden outputs with tolerance threshold.

- Example curl smoke test:
  ```bash
  for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"Hello world"}' https://api.cluster.example.com/v1/generate | jq '.output'; done
  ```

9) Communications and escalation
- During maintenance windows or incidents:
  - Primary incident channel: #infra-private-deployments (Slack).
  - Pager: Oncall SRE (see roster in eng-sre/runbooks).
  - Status page: update with progress and ETA for rollback/restore activities.

- Post-incident: open a postmortem in confluence under oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems and link to this doc. Include timeline, impact, mitigations, and remediation plan.

10) Ownership and SLAs
- Recommended owners:
  - Installation & upgrades: Solutions Engineering (primary) + Customer Infra (co-owner).
  - Day-2 SRE: Customer Success SRE (primary) and Redwood Platform SRE (support).
  - Security & compliance signoff: Security team (owner).

- SLA guidance for private deployments: availability 99.9% (commercial SLA to be defined per contract). Support response times per tier documented in pricing-and-packaging.

Appendix A: Compatibility matrix (summary)
- k8s supported versions: 1.24, 1.25, 1.26 (validate before any major upgrade).
- GPU driver / CUDA matrix: see eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/quantization-profiles for detailed mapping.

Appendix B: Useful commands and artifacts
- Preflight: ./preflight.sh --config=mycluster.yaml
- Snapshot DB: pg_dump -Fc -h $DB_HOST -U redwood redwood_metadata > metadata.$(date +%F).dump
- Restore DB (example): pg_restore -c -d redwood -h standby-db -U redwood metadata.2026-02-09.dump
